source.text: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ δι’ ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἐν οἴκῳ ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: And having entered again into Capernaum after days it was heard that in [a] house he is.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had entered Capernaum again after [some] days, it was heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was at home.
en.B: Some days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to Capernaum, and word got around that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was at home.
en.R: After a few days Jesus returned to the town of Capernaum. People heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was staying at a house there.

es.L: Y habiendo entrado otra vez en Cafarnaúm después de [algunos] días, se oyó que estaba en casa.
es.B: Algunos días después volvió a Cafarnaúm, y se corrió la voz de que estaba en casa.
es.R: Unos días más tarde, Jesús regresó al pueblo de Cafarnaúm. La gente supo que estaba alojado en una casa de allí.

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kuingia tena Kapernaumu baada ya siku [kadhaa], ilisikika kwamba yuko nyumbani.
sw.B: Siku kadhaa baadaye alirudi Kapernaumu, na habari zikaenea kwamba yuko nyumbani.
sw.R: Baada ya siku chache Yesu alirudi katika mji wa Kapernaumu. Watu walisikia kwamba alikuwa akikaa katika nyumba moja huko.

decisions.choice: in a house: at home, most likely Simon's house (1:29)
decisions.reason: The phrase means "indoors" or "at home". Capernaum had become Jesus' base, and Simon's house is the last house named (1:29).

decisions.choice: after days: after some days
decisions.reason: The phrase gives no number. Jesus had been away preaching in the towns of Galilee (1:38-39).

decisions.choice: it was heard: people heard and passed it on
decisions.reason: The passive "it was heard" means the news spread.

decisions.choice: staying at a house there
decisions.reason: Readable does not say whose home it was, since Mark does not.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (él, lo, le, su, sus, tus, mi), not on the verb ending (estaba)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("sígueme"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English, as in Mark 16. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on yuko (he is); spans only on free pronouns and possessives (naye, wake, yake)
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the subject prefix of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark 16. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον.

records.literal_gloss: And were gathered many, so that no longer to have room not even the [space] at the door, and he was speaking to them the word.

en.L: And many were gathered together, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking the word to them.
en.B: So many people crowded in that there was no space left, even outside the door, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke the word to them.
en.R: So many people came that the house was full. There was no room left, even outside the door. Jesus was telling them God's message.

es.L: Y se reunieron muchos, de modo que ya no había lugar, ni siquiera junto a la puerta; y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les hablaba la palabra.
es.B: Se juntó tanta gente que ya no quedaba sitio ni siquiera delante de la puerta, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les anunciaba la palabra.
es.R: Llegó tanta gente que la casa se llenó. Ya no cabía nadie, ni siquiera afuera, junto a la puerta. Jesús les estaba enseñando el mensaje de Dios.

sw.L: Na wengi wakakusanyika, hata pasiwe na nafasi tena, wala hata mlangoni; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alikuwa akiwaambia neno.
sw.B: Watu wengi sana walikusanyika hata pakawa hakuna nafasi tena, hata nje ya mlango; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawahubiria neno.
sw.R: Watu wengi walikuja hata nyumba ikajaa. Hapakuwa na nafasi tena, hata nje ya mlango. Yesu alikuwa akiwaeleza ujumbe wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: the word: God's message, the good news Jesus proclaimed
decisions.reason: "The word" is the message of 1:14-15. Mark uses it for Jesus' preaching (4:14, 33).

decisions.choice: not even at the door: the crowd filled the doorway and the space outside
alternatives: no one could reach the door
decisions.reason: Houses opened onto a small courtyard or the street; even that space was full, which is why the four take another way in (2:4).

decisions.choice: he was speaking: he was teaching when what follows happened
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous and sets the scene.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says whose word it is, since "the word" alone means little to new readers.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχονται φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων.

records.literal_gloss: And they come bringing to him a paralytic being carried by four.

en.L: And they come, bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a paralytic carried by four [men].
en.B: Then some people arrived with a paralyzed man for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, carried by four of them.
en.R: Four men came carrying a man who could not move his body. They wanted to bring him to Jesus.

es.L: Y vienen trayendo hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a un paralítico llevado por cuatro [hombres].
es.B: Entonces llegaron unas personas que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traían a un paralítico; lo cargaban entre cuatro.
es.R: Cuatro hombres llegaron cargando a un hombre que no podía mover el cuerpo. Querían llevarlo hasta Jesús.

sw.L: Na wanakuja wakimletea mtu aliyepooza, akibebwa na [watu] wanne.
sw.B: Kisha watu fulani walifika wakimletea mtu aliyepooza, akiwa amebebwa na wanne kati yao.
sw.R: Watu wanne walikuja wakiwa wamembeba mtu ambaye hakuweza kuusogeza mwili wake. Walitaka kumpeleka kwa Yesu.

decisions.choice: a paralytic: a man who could not move part or all of his body
alternatives: a man who was very weak
decisions.reason: He had to be carried on a mat (2:4).

decisions.choice: they come ... carried by four: a group, four of whom carried him
decisions.reason: "They" may be the four, or a larger group with four bearers. The faith Jesus sees (2:5) is theirs.

decisions.choice: they come: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: four [men] (L); four men (R)
decisions.reason: "Four" in Greek is masculine, so English supplies "men".

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (vienen); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (llegaron)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of his story in the present (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanakuja); past at Balanced and Readable (walifika, walikuja)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of his story in the present (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν, καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο.

records.literal_gloss: And not being able to bring [him] near to him because of the crowd, they unroofed the roof where he was, and having dug [it] out they let down the mat where the paralytic was lying.

en.L: And not being able to bring [him] near to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the crowd, they unroofed the roof where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, and having dug through [it], they let down the mat on which the paralytic was lying.
en.B: The crowd kept them from getting him near Jesus, so they took off part of the roof above where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. They broke through it and lowered the mat with the paralyzed man lying on it.
en.R: But there were too many people, and they could not get him close to Jesus. So they climbed up and made a hole in the roof above {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then they let the man down on his mat.

es.L: Y, no pudiendo acercar[lo] a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a causa de la multitud, quitaron el techo donde estaba y, tras perforar[lo], bajan la camilla en que yacía el paralítico.
es.B: Como no podían acercarlo a Jesús por causa de la multitud, quitaron parte del techo justo encima de donde estaba. Abrieron un hueco y bajaron la camilla con el paralítico acostado en ella.
es.R: Pero había demasiada gente y no podían acercarlo a Jesús. Así que subieron al techo e hicieron un agujero encima de donde estaba {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Luego bajaron al hombre en su camilla.

sw.L: Na wasipoweza kumfikisha karibu {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kwa sababu ya umati, waliondoa paa juu ya mahali alipokuwa, na wakiisha kulitoboa, wanaushusha mkeka aliokuwa amelalia yule aliyepooza.
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya umati hawakuweza kumfikisha kwa Yesu, basi waliondoa sehemu ya paa juu ya mahali alipokuwa. Wakalitoboa, wakaushusha mkeka ambao yule aliyepooza alikuwa amelala juu yake.
sw.R: Lakini watu walikuwa wengi mno, na hawakuweza kumfikisha karibu na Yesu. Basi walipanda juu ya nyumba, wakatoboa tundu katika paa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Kisha wakamshusha yule mtu akiwa juu ya mkeka wake.

decisions.choice: the roof: a flat roof of beams, branches and packed clay
decisions.reason: Houses in Galilee had flat roofs reached by an outside stair. The four could dig through the clay and branches between the beams. Luke 5:19 mentions tiles, as in houses he knew.

decisions.choice: mat: a poor person's pallet or bedroll
decisions.reason: The word is a simple mattress that a man could roll up and carry (2:11-12).

decisions.choice: bring near: bring him to Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bringing someone or something to a person. The object, the paralyzed man, is understood.

decisions.choice: climbed up
decisions.reason: Readable says how they got to the roof, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: camilla
decisions.reason: As in John 5:8, for the same word: a poor person's light bedding that could be carried (meaning decision m2). "Lecho" and "cama" suggest furniture too heavy to lower through a roof.

decisions.choice: mkeka
decisions.reason: As in John 5:8, for the same word: a poor person's light bedding that could be rolled up and carried (meaning decision m2). "Godoro" (mattress) and "kitanda" (bed) are too heavy to lower through a roof.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Τέκνον, ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the Jesus the faith of them he says to the paralytic, Child, are forgiven of you the sins.

en.L: And Jesus, seeing their faith, says to the paralytic, "Child, your sins are forgiven."
en.B: Jesus saw how they trusted in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "My child, your sins are forgiven."
en.R: Jesus saw that they had faith in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man who could not move, "My child, God forgives your sins."

es.L: Y Jesús, al ver la fe de ellos, dice al paralítico: «Hijo, son perdonados tus pecados».
es.B: Jesús vio cuánto confiaban en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y le dijo al paralítico: «Hijo mío, tus pecados quedan perdonados».
es.R: Jesús vio que tenían fe en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Entonces le dijo al hombre que no podía moverse: «Hijo mío, Dios te perdona tus pecados».

sw.L: Na Yesu akiona imani yao, anamwambia aliyepooza, "Mwanangu, zinasamehewa dhambi zako."
sw.B: Yesu alipoona jinsi walivyomtumaini, alimwambia yule aliyepooza, "Mwanangu, dhambi zako zimesamehewa."
sw.R: Yesu aliona kwamba walikuwa na imani {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Basi akamwambia yule mtu asiyeweza kujisogeza, "Mwanangu, Mungu anakusamehe dhambi zako."

decisions.choice: their faith: the faith of the four and of the man himself
decisions.reason: "Their" most naturally includes those who carried him and the man they carried. Their effort showed that they trusted Jesus to help.

decisions.choice: child: a warm way to speak to someone
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks as a father or teacher would. It says nothing about the man's age.

decisions.choice: are forgiven: God forgives, and Jesus says so now
decisions.reason: The passive often means God is the one acting. Jesus declares the forgiveness as done, which the scribes take as claiming God's right (2:7).

decisions.choice: forgiveness first: the man's deepest need
alternatives: his illness was a punishment for sin
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of sins before healing. Mark does not say that the illness was caused by sin; Jesus heals and forgives as signs of the same authority (2:10-11).

decisions.choice: trusted in him (B); had faith in him (R)
decisions.reason: "Saw their faith" sounds odd in English, since faith is not seen. Balanced and Readable say what was seen. Readable keeps the key word faith.

decisions.choice: God forgives your sins
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Hijo (L); Hijo mío (B, R)
decisions.reason: A warm way to address the man (meaning decision m2). "Niño" would sound as if he were a boy; "hijo" is how an older person speaks kindly to a younger one in Spanish.

decisions.choice: Mwanangu (my child)
decisions.reason: A warm way to address the man (meaning decision m2). "Mtoto" alone would sound as if he were a small boy; "mwanangu" is how an older person speaks kindly to a younger one.

decisions.choice: zinasamehewa (are being forgiven) at Literal; zimesamehewa (have been forgiven) at Balanced
decisions.reason: God forgives, and Jesus says so now (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the Greek present; Balanced uses the perfect, the usual Swahili way to announce something done and standing. Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἦσαν δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐκεῖ καθήμενοι καὶ διαλογιζόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Were now some of the scribes there sitting and reasoning in the hearts of them,

en.L: Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
en.B: Some of the scribes were sitting there, and they were asking themselves,
en.R: Some teachers of God's law were sitting there. They thought to themselves,

es.L: Y había allí algunos de los escribas sentados y razonando en sus corazones:
es.B: Estaban sentados allí algunos de los escribas, que se preguntaban para sí:
es.R: Algunos maestros de la ley estaban sentados allí. Pensaban para sí:

sw.L: Basi huko walikuwa wameketi baadhi ya waandishi, wakitafakari ndani ya mioyo yao,
sw.B: Baadhi ya waandishi walikuwa wameketi pale, nao wakajiuliza moyoni,
sw.R: Baadhi ya walimu wa sheria walikuwa wameketi pale. Walifikiri ndani yao,

decisions.choice: the scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: As in 1:22. They are present as teachers, sitting while others stand.

decisions.choice: reasoning in their hearts: thinking it over, without saying it aloud
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and decides. They do not speak, but Jesus knows their thoughts (2:8).

decisions.choice: teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:22.

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Literal and Balanced keep the title "escribas"; Readable says what these men were, teachers of the law (meaning decision m1), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Literal and Balanced keep the title, "waandishi"; Readable says what these men were, teachers of the law (meaning decision m1), as the English Readable does.

source.text: Τί οὗτος οὕτως λαλεῖ;

records.literal_gloss: Why this [one] thus speaks?

en.L: "Why does this [man] speak like this?
en.B: "Why does this fellow talk this way?
en.R: "How can this man say things like that?

es.L: «¿Por qué este [hombre] habla así?
es.B: «¿Por qué habla así este individuo?
es.R: «¿Cómo puede este hombre decir cosas así?

sw.L: "Kwa nini huyu [mtu] anaongea hivyo?
sw.B: "Mbona mtu huyu anazungumza namna hii?
sw.R: "Mtu huyu anawezaje kusema maneno kama hayo?

decisions.choice: this one: said with contempt
decisions.reason: They do not use his name. "This one" can be scornful, as the next words show.

decisions.choice: this [man] (L); this fellow (B)
decisions.reason: Greek needs no noun; English does. Balanced keeps the scorn with "fellow".

decisions.choice: este individuo
decisions.reason: The Greek "this one" is said with contempt (meaning decision m1). Spanish "individuo" carries the same coolness, as the English "this fellow" does; "este hombre" would be neutral.

source.text: βλασφημεῖ· τίς δύναται ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός;

records.literal_gloss: He blasphemes; who is able to forgive sins except one, the God?

en.L: He blasphemes! Who is able to forgive sins except one, God?"
en.B: It is blasphemy! Who but God alone can forgive sins?"
en.R: He is insulting God! Only God can forgive sins!"

es.L: ¡Blasfema! ¿Quién puede perdonar pecados sino uno, Dios?».
es.B: ¡Eso es blasfemia! ¿Quién puede perdonar pecados, sino solo Dios?».
es.R: ¡Está insultando a Dios! ¡Solo Dios puede perdonar pecados!».

sw.L: Anakufuru! Ni nani mwenye uwezo wa kusamehe dhambi, ila mmoja tu, Mungu?"
sw.B: Huku ni kukufuru! Ni nani anayeweza kusamehe dhambi isipokuwa Mungu peke yake?"
sw.R: Anamtukana Mungu! Mungu peke yake ndiye anayeweza kusamehe dhambi!"

decisions.choice: blasphemes: insults God by claiming what is God's alone
decisions.reason: To blaspheme is to speak against God. They hold that Jesus takes God's place by forgiving sins. The same charge brings his death sentence (14:64).

decisions.choice: except one, God: recalls the confession that God is one
alternatives: only a way of saying alone
decisions.reason: "One" echoes the Shema, "the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4), which Jesus quotes in 12:29. Only God forgives sins (Isaiah 43:25).

decisions.choice: who is able...? a question that expects the answer: no one
decisions.reason: The question is rhetorical; they are sure no one but God can do it.

decisions.choice: He blasphemes (L); It is blasphemy (B); He is insulting God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb. Readable says plainly what blaspheming is.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐπιγνοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως διαλογίζονται ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having known the Jesus in the spirit of him that thus they are reasoning within themselves he says to them, Why these things are you reasoning in the hearts of you?

en.L: And immediately Jesus, knowing in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit that they were reasoning like this within themselves, says to them, "Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
en.B: At once Jesus knew in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit what they were thinking. "Why do you turn these things over in your hearts?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them.
en.R: Right away Jesus knew in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit what they were thinking. He said to them, "Why are you thinking these things?

es.L: Y en seguida Jesús, conociendo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu que razonaban así dentro de sí mismos, les dice: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:razonan|razonáis}} estas cosas en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones?
es.B: Al instante Jesús supo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu lo que estaban pensando. «¿Por qué {{plural_you:le dan|le dais}} vueltas a esto en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón?», les preguntó.
es.R: En ese mismo momento Jesús supo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu lo que estaban pensando. Les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} esas cosas?

sw.L: Na mara Yesu, akijua katika roho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwamba wanawaza hivyo ndani yao, anawaambia, "Kwa nini mnawaza mambo haya mioyoni mwenu?
sw.B: Mara moja Yesu alijua katika roho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} walichokuwa wakiwaza. "Mbona mnayatafakari mambo haya mioyoni mwenu?" akawauliza.
sw.R: Papo hapo Yesu alijua katika roho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} walichokuwa wakifikiri. Akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnafikiri mambo kama hayo?

decisions.choice: in his spirit: in his own inner self
decisions.reason: "His spirit" is Jesus' own spirit, his inner life. He knows their thoughts without being told, as God does (1 Samuel 16:7).

decisions.choice: knowing: knowing fully, perceiving
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one: he knew for certain.

decisions.choice: why...? a challenge, not a request for information
decisions.reason: Jesus goes on at once with his own question (2:9).

decisions.choice: the question, then "he asked them" (B)
alternatives: he says to them, then the question
decisions.reason: Balanced closes the quotation here, so the next question (2:9) opens its own.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the words addressed to the scribes (razonan|razonáis, sus|vuestros)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them, with "ustedes" as the default. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει;

records.literal_gloss: Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, Are forgiven of you the sins, or to say, Rise and take up the mat of you and walk?

en.L: Which is easier: to say to the paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Rise, and take up your mat, and walk'?
en.B: "What is easier to say to this paralyzed man: 'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up, take your mat, and walk'?
en.R: Is it easier to tell this man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to tell him, 'Stand up, take your mat, and walk'?

es.L: ¿Qué es más fácil: decir al paralítico: “Son perdonados tus pecados”, o decir: “Levántate, y toma tu camilla, y anda”?
es.B: «¿Qué es más fácil decirle a este paralítico: “Tus pecados quedan perdonados”, o “Levántate, toma tu camilla y anda”?
es.R: ¿Qué es más fácil decirle a este hombre: “Tus pecados están perdonados”, o decirle: “Ponte de pie, toma tu camilla y camina”?

sw.L: Ni lipi lililo rahisi zaidi, kumwambia aliyepooza, 'Zinasamehewa dhambi zako,' au kusema, 'Inuka, na uchukue mkeka wako, na utembee'?
sw.B: "Ni lipi rahisi zaidi kumwambia mtu huyu aliyepooza: 'Dhambi zako zimesamehewa,' au 'Simama, chukua mkeka wako, utembee'?
sw.R: Je, ni rahisi zaidi kumwambia mtu huyu, 'Dhambi zako zimesamehewa,' au kumwambia, 'Simama, chukua mkeka wako, utembee'?

decisions.choice: which is easier? it is easier to say the words that cannot be checked
decisions.reason: Anyone can say "your sins are forgiven", since no one can see whether it happened. Saying "get up and walk" is tested at once. The healing will show that his first word was true (2:10).

decisions.choice: rise: get up
decisions.reason: The verb is the everyday word for getting up, also used of rising from death (16:6). Here the man gets up from his mat (2:12).

source.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ·

records.literal_gloss: That but you may know that authority has the Son of the man on the earth to forgive sins, he says to the paralytic,

en.L: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins"—{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the paralytic—
en.B: But I want you to be sure of this: the Son of Man has the right on earth to forgive sins." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned to the paralyzed man.
en.R: I will show you that the Son of Man has the power here on earth to forgive sins." Then Jesus spoke to the man who could not move.

es.L: Pero para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que el Hijo del Hombre tiene autoridad en la tierra para perdonar pecados» —dice al paralítico—:
es.B: Pero quiero que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} con certeza esto: el Hijo del Hombre tiene derecho a perdonar pecados en la tierra». Entonces se volvió hacia el paralítico.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} voy a mostrar que el Hijo del Hombre tiene poder aquí en la tierra para perdonar pecados». Entonces Jesús le habló al hombre que no podía moverse.

sw.L: Lakini ili mjue kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka duniani ya kusamehe dhambi"—anamwambia aliyepooza—
sw.B: Lakini nataka mjue hakika kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka duniani ya kusamehe dhambi." Kisha akamgeukia yule aliyepooza.
sw.R: Nitawaonyesha kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana uwezo hapa duniani wa kusamehe dhambi." Kisha Yesu akasema na yule mtu asiyeweza kujisogeza.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Mark this is how Jesus speaks of himself. In Daniel 7 one like a son of man receives authority from God, which fits the claim here.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power
decisions.reason: The same word as in 1:22 and 1:27. Jesus claims on earth the right that the scribes say belongs to God in heaven.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: Jesus stops speaking to the scribes and turns to the man
alternatives: Mark's own comment to his readers
decisions.reason: The words "he says to the paralytic" break into Jesus' sentence. Some read the first half as Mark speaking to his readers, but it most likely continues Jesus' answer to the scribes.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: This is a title, as at John 1:51, so it keeps its familiar form.

decisions.choice: Then he turned to (B); Then Jesus spoke to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable close the sentence first, so the reader is not left in a broken one.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre, with capitals as a title
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, as in John: the title Jesus uses of himself, with the figure of Daniel 7 behind it (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: autoridad (L); derecho (B); poder (R)
decisions.reason: The word means both the right and the power to act (meaning decision m2). Each level follows the English word for it; Spanish has no single word that holds both.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, used in John and across the New Testament drafts (meaning decision m1). "Mwana wa Mtu" is closer to the Greek words; a reviewer may weigh it.

decisions.choice: mamlaka (L, B); uwezo (R)
decisions.reason: The word means both the right and the power to act (meaning decision m2). "Mamlaka" holds both; Readable says "uwezo" (power), as the English Readable does. "Haki" is kept for righteousness.

source.text: Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: To you I say, rise, take up the mat of you and go to the house of you.

en.L: "To you I say, rise, take up your mat, and go to your home."
en.B: "Get up, I tell you. Take your mat and go home."
en.R: He said, "Stand up! Take your mat and go home!"

es.L: «A ti te digo: levántate, toma tu camilla y vete a tu casa».
es.B: «Levántate, te digo. Toma tu camilla y vete a tu casa».
es.R: Le dijo: «¡Ponte de pie! ¡Toma tu camilla y vete a casa!».

sw.L: "Wewe nakuambia, inuka, chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani kwako."
sw.B: "Simama, nakuambia. Chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani."
sw.R: Akasema, "Simama! Chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani!"

decisions.choice: to you I say: "you" stands first for emphasis
decisions.reason: After speaking to the scribes, Jesus speaks to the man himself.

decisions.choice: rise, take up, go: the command that heals
decisions.reason: The man can do what he is told only if he has been healed.

source.text: καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ εὐθὺς ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ἔμπροσθεν πάντων, ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι Οὕτως οὐδέποτε εἴδομεν.

records.literal_gloss: And he rose and immediately having taken up the mat he went out before all, so that all were amazed and glorified the God saying, Thus never we saw.

en.L: And he rose, and immediately, taking up the mat, he went out in front of everyone, so that all were amazed and glorified God, saying, "We never saw [anything] like this!"
en.B: He got up, picked up his mat at once, and walked out while they all watched. They were all astonished and gave glory to God. "We have never seen anything like it!" they said.
en.R: The man got up. Right away he took his mat and went out where everyone could see him. All the people were amazed, and they praised God. They said, "We have never seen anything like this!"

es.L: Y se levantó y, en seguida, tomando la camilla, salió delante de todos, de modo que todos estaban asombrados y glorificaban a Dios, diciendo: «¡Nunca vimos [cosa] así!».
es.B: Él se levantó, tomó en seguida su camilla y salió a la vista de todos. Todos quedaron asombrados y dieron gloria a Dios. «¡Nunca hemos visto nada parecido!», decían.
es.R: El hombre se levantó. Enseguida tomó su camilla y salió donde todos lo podían ver. Toda la gente estaba asombrada, y alababan a Dios. Decían: «¡Nunca hemos visto algo como esto!».

sw.L: Naye akainuka, na mara akichukua mkeka, akatoka mbele ya wote, hata wote wakashangaa, wakamtukuza Mungu, wakisema, "Namna hii hatukuwahi kuona!"
sw.B: Aliinuka, mara akachukua mkeka wake, akatoka nje wote wakimtazama. Wote wakastaajabu, wakamtukuza Mungu. "Hatujawahi kuona kitu kama hiki!" wakasema.
sw.R: Yule mtu alisimama. Mara moja akachukua mkeka wake, akatoka nje mahali ambapo kila mtu angeweza kumwona. Watu wote walishangaa, wakamsifu Mungu. Walisema, "Hatujawahi kuona jambo kama hili!"

decisions.choice: went out before all: in plain sight of the crowd
decisions.reason: The crowd that blocked the door now sees him walk out through it.

decisions.choice: glorified God: praised God for what he had done
decisions.reason: The crowd gives the glory to God, whose work they see in Jesus.

decisions.choice: all: the whole crowd, perhaps the scribes too
alternatives: only the people, not the scribes
decisions.reason: Mark does not separate the scribes from the rest here.

decisions.choice: praised God
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday verb with the same meaning.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And he went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd was coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them.
en.B: Once more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out along the lakeshore. The whole crowd kept coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them.
en.R: Jesus went to the shore of Lake Galilee again. A big crowd gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them.

es.L: Y salió otra vez junto al mar; y toda la multitud venía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y les enseñaba.
es.B: Una vez más salió a la orilla del lago. Toda la multitud seguía acudiendo a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y les enseñaba.
es.R: Jesús fue otra vez a la orilla del lago de Galilea. Mucha gente se reunió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les enseñaba.

sw.L: Na akatoka tena kando ya bahari; na umati wote ukawa ukimjia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawa akiwafundisha.
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine alitoka akaenda kando ya ziwa. Umati wote ukawa ukimjia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawafundisha.
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda tena ufuoni mwa Ziwa Galilaya. Umati mkubwa wa watu ulikusanyika kumzunguka, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawafundisha.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, a lake
decisions.reason: As in 1:16. Capernaum stood on its shore.

decisions.choice: was coming, was teaching: a stream of people and a time of teaching
decisions.reason: Both verbs are continuous.

decisions.choice: lakeshore (B); Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake, as at 1:16.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: the "sea" is the Lake of Galilee (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps Mark's word; Balanced and Readable say lake, as the English does.

decisions.choice: bahari (L); ziwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: the "sea" is the Lake of Galilee (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps Mark's word; Balanced and Readable say lake, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: And passing by he saw Levi the [son] of the Alphaeus sitting at the tax office, and he says to him, Follow me.

en.L: And passing by, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Levi the [son] of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} walked along, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} caught sight of Levi son of Alphaeus sitting in the tax office. "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him.
en.R: As Jesus was walking along, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a man named Levi, the son of Alphaeus. Levi was sitting at the place where he collected taxes. Jesus said to him, "Come with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} follower."

es.L: Y al pasar, vio a Leví, el [hijo] de Alfeo, sentado en el puesto de impuestos, y le dice: «Sígueme».
es.B: Mientras caminaba, vio a Leví, hijo de Alfeo, sentado en su puesto de cobro de impuestos. «Sígueme», le dijo.
es.R: Mientras Jesús iba caminando, vio a un hombre llamado Leví, hijo de Alfeo. Leví estaba sentado en el lugar donde cobraba los impuestos. Jesús le dijo: «Ven conmigo y sé {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} discípulo».

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akipita, alimwona Lawi [mwana] wa Alfayo ameketi kwenye kibanda cha ushuru, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anamwambia, "Nifuate."
sw.B: Alipokuwa akipita, alimwona Lawi mwana wa Alfayo ameketi katika kibanda cha ushuru. Akamwambia, "Nifuate."
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akitembea, alimwona mtu mmoja jina lake Lawi, mwana wa Alfayo. Lawi alikuwa ameketi mahali alipokuwa akitoza ushuru. Yesu akamwambia, "Njoo pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, uwe mwanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: the tax office: a booth where tolls and taxes were collected
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on a trade road near a border, and goods passing through were taxed. Collectors worked for Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee, or for those who bought the right to collect. Many people saw them as cheats and traitors.

decisions.choice: Levi: the same man the Gospel of Matthew calls Matthew
decisions.reason: Matthew 9:9 tells the same story about a tax collector named Matthew. Mark's list of the twelve names a Matthew but no Levi (3:18), so he may have had two names.

decisions.choice: follow me: become my disciple
come with me and be my follower
decisions.reason: Readable says what following means.

decisions.choice: sé mi discípulo
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "discípulo" at every level, even where the English Readable says "follower" (meaning decision m3). The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: uwe mwanafunzi wangu (be my disciple)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "mwanafunzi" at every level, even where the English Readable says "follower" (meaning decision m3). The same through the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having risen he followed him.

en.L: And rising, he followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He got up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Levi got up and went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y, poniéndose de pie, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.
es.B: Él se levantó y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.
es.R: Leví se levantó y se fue con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Naye akainuka, akamfuata.
sw.B: Lawi aliinuka, akamfuata.
sw.R: Lawi alisimama, akaenda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: rising, he followed: he left his work at once
decisions.reason: Like the fishermen (1:18), he leaves his trade at a word.

source.text: Καὶ γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And it comes to pass him to recline in the house of him, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with the Jesus and the disciples of him; there were for many, and they were following him.

en.L: And it happens that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is reclining at table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, for there were many, and they were following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Later Jesus was having a meal in Levi's house, and many tax collectors and sinners shared the table with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. There were many such people among those who followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Later Jesus ate a meal at Levi's house. Many tax collectors and other people known as sinners ate there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. Many people like that were following Jesus.

es.L: Y sucede que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está recostado [a la mesa] en su casa, y muchos publicanos y pecadores estaban recostados [a la mesa] con Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, porque eran muchos, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían.
es.B: Más tarde, Jesús estaba comiendo en casa de Leví, y muchos cobradores de impuestos y pecadores compartían la mesa con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Había muchos de ellos entre los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían.
es.R: Después, Jesús comió en la casa de Leví. Muchos cobradores de impuestos y otros a quienes la gente llamaba pecadores comieron allí con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Muchas personas así seguían a Jesús.

sw.L: Na inatokea kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ameegemea [mezani] nyumbani mwake, na watoza ushuru wengi na wenye dhambi walikuwa wameegemea [mezani] pamoja na Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}; kwa maana walikuwa wengi, nao walikuwa wakimfuata.
sw.B: Baadaye Yesu alikuwa akila chakula nyumbani kwa Lawi, na watoza ushuru wengi na wenye dhambi wakala pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Watu wa namna hiyo walikuwa wengi miongoni mwa wale waliomfuata.
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu alikula chakula nyumbani kwa Lawi. Watoza ushuru wengi na watu wengine waliojulikana kuwa wenye dhambi walikula pale pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Watu wengi wa namna hiyo walikuwa wakimfuata Yesu.

decisions.choice: his house: Levi's house
decisions.reason: "His" could be Jesus or Levi. Luke 5:29 says Levi gave a great feast in his house, which fits the call that comes just before.

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on couches at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on their sides around a low table. Eating together meant friendship and acceptance.

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for breaking the law, or who did not keep it as the Pharisees taught
decisions.reason: The word marks people that religious Jews kept away from: those with a bad name, and those careless of the law's purity rules.

decisions.choice: there were many, and they followed him: many such people were among his followers
alternatives: there were many disciples, who followed him
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean that many tax collectors and sinners followed Jesus, or that his disciples were many. This is the first time Mark uses the word disciples.

decisions.choice: Levi's house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the house's owner, following the meaning note.

decisions.choice: other people known as sinners
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "sinners" is a label others gave them.

decisions.choice: publicanos (L); cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Literal keeps the traditional name, "publicanos"; Balanced and Readable say what these men did, which most readers no longer know from the old word.

decisions.choice: recostado [a la mesa]
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the posture and brackets the table, as Matthew 9:10 does; Balanced and Readable say that they ate together.

decisions.choice: watoza ushuru
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, at every level: "those who collect duty", which says what these men did.

decisions.choice: ameegemea [mezani] (reclining [at table])
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision m2). "Kuegemea" is to lean or recline; Literal keeps the posture and brackets the table, as in Mark 16:14. Balanced and Readable say that they ate together.

source.text: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τῶν Φαρισαίων ἰδόντες ὅτι ἐσθίει μετὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει;

records.literal_gloss: And the scribes of the Pharisees having seen that he eats with the sinners and tax collectors were saying to the disciples of him, Why with the tax collectors and sinners does he eat?

en.L: And the scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, were saying to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
en.B: Some scribes who were Pharisees saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} eating with sinners and tax collectors, and they asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} eating with tax collectors and sinners?"
en.R: Some teachers of God's law who were Pharisees saw this. They asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} share meals with tax collectors and sinners?"

es.L: Y los escribas de los fariseos, viendo que comía con los pecadores y publicanos, decían a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Por qué con los publicanos y pecadores come?».
es.B: Algunos escribas que eran fariseos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron comer con pecadores y cobradores de impuestos, y preguntaron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Por qué come con cobradores de impuestos y pecadores?».
es.R: Algunos maestros de la ley que eran fariseos vieron esto. Preguntaron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Por qué se sienta {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a comer con cobradores de impuestos y pecadores?».

sw.L: Na waandishi wa Mafarisayo, walipoona kwamba anakula pamoja na wenye dhambi na watoza ushuru, walikuwa wakiwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Mbona pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi anakula?"
sw.B: Baadhi ya waandishi waliokuwa Mafarisayo walimwona akila pamoja na wenye dhambi na watoza ushuru, wakawauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kwa nini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anakula pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya walimu wa sheria waliokuwa Mafarisayo waliona jambo hilo. Wakawauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kwa nini anashiriki chakula na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi?"

decisions.choice: the scribes of the Pharisees: scribes who belonged to the Pharisees
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were a movement devoted to keeping the law exactly, including rules of purity at meals. Some scribes belonged to them.

decisions.choice: a question: why does he eat with them?
alternatives: a statement: he eats with tax collectors and sinners!
decisions.reason: The Greek word that opens the saying can introduce a question or a statement. The SBLGNT punctuates it as a question.

decisions.choice: eating with them: sharing a meal meant accepting them
alternatives: only being in the same room
decisions.reason: To the Pharisees, eating with such people made a teacher unclean and approved their way of life.

decisions.choice: teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:22.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλ’ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες· οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the Jesus says to them, Not need have the [ones] being strong of a physician but the [ones] badly having; not I came to call righteous but sinners.

en.L: And hearing [this], Jesus says to them, "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I did not come to call righteous [people], but sinners."
en.B: Jesus heard it and told them, "People who are well do not need a doctor; sick people do. I came to call sinners, not the righteous."
en.R: Jesus heard what they said. He told them, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people do. I did not come to invite good people. I came to invite sinners."

es.L: Y al oír[lo], Jesús les dice: «No tienen necesidad de médico los fuertes, sino los que están mal; no vine a llamar a justos, sino a pecadores».
es.B: Jesús lo oyó y les dijo: «Los que están sanos no necesitan médico; los enfermos, sí. Vine a llamar a los pecadores, no a los justos».
es.R: Jesús oyó lo que decían, y les dijo: «Las personas sanas no necesitan un médico. Los enfermos sí. Yo no vine a invitar a los buenos. Vine a invitar a los pecadores».

sw.L: Na Yesu aliposikia, anawaambia, "Wenye nguvu hawana haja ya tabibu, bali walio hali mbaya; sikuja kuwaita watu wenye haki, ila wenye dhambi."
sw.B: Yesu aliposikia, aliwaambia, "Walio wazima hawahitaji daktari; wagonjwa ndio wanaomhitaji. Nilikuja kuwaita wenye dhambi, si wenye haki."
sw.R: Yesu alisikia waliyosema. Akawaambia, "Watu wenye afya hawahitaji daktari. Wagonjwa ndio wanaomhitaji. Sikuja kuwaalika watu wema. Nilikuja kuwaalika wenye dhambi."

decisions.choice: the strong do not need a physician: a common saying
decisions.reason: Jesus uses a proverb: a doctor goes where the sick are. So he goes to sinners.

decisions.choice: to call: to invite, as to a meal, and to summon to the kingdom
decisions.reason: The word is used for inviting guests to a feast and for Jesus' call to follow him (1:20).

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who think themselves right with God, or are thought so
alternatives: people who truly need nothing from God
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks in the scribes' own terms. He does not say there are people who need no repentance.

decisions.choice: good people
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for those who were counted righteous.

source.text: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες.

records.literal_gloss: And were the disciples of John and the Pharisees fasting.

en.L: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting.
en.B: John's disciples and the Pharisees were keeping a fast.
en.R: At that time John's followers and the Pharisees were fasting. They went without food for a time to worship God.

es.L: Y los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban ayunando.
es.B: Los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban guardando un ayuno.
es.R: En ese tiempo, los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban ayunando. Pasaban un tiempo sin comer para adorar a Dios.

sw.L: Na wanafunzi wa Yohana na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakifunga.
sw.B: Wanafunzi wa Yohana na Mafarisayo walikuwa katika kipindi cha kufunga.
sw.R: Wakati huo wanafunzi wa Yohana na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakifunga. Waliacha kula kwa muda ili kumwabudu Mungu.

decisions.choice: fasting: going without food as a religious act
decisions.reason: The law set one fast a year, on the Day of Atonement. Pharisees also fasted twice a week (Luke 18:12). Fasting went with prayer, mourning and repentance.

decisions.choice: were fasting: they were keeping a fast at the time
decisions.reason: The words may describe a fast going on that day, or their regular practice.

decisions.choice: went without food for a time to worship God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what fasting is.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν, οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: And they come and say to him, Because of why the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but the your disciples not fast?

en.L: And they come and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples do not fast?"
en.B: People came and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "John's disciples fast, and so do the Pharisees' disciples. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not fast?"
en.R: Some people came to Jesus and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "John's followers and the Pharisees' followers fast. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers not fast?"

es.L: Y vienen y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «¿Por qué los discípulos de Juan y los discípulos de los fariseos ayunan, pero {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no ayunan?».
es.B: Algunos vinieron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Los discípulos de Juan ayunan, y también los discípulos de los fariseos. ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no ayunan?».
es.R: Algunas personas fueron a ver a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Los discípulos de Juan y los de los fariseos ayunan. ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no ayunan?».

sw.L: Na wanakuja na kumwambia, "Kwa nini wanafunzi wa Yohana na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo hufunga, lakini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawafungi?"
sw.B: Watu fulani walikuja, wakamwuliza, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana hufunga, na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo pia. Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawafungi?"
sw.R: Watu fulani walimwendea Yesu, wakamwuliza, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo hufunga. Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawafungi?"

decisions.choice: they come: some people, not named
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who asked. Matthew 9:14 says it was John's disciples.

decisions.choice: your disciples: a teacher was answerable for his disciples
decisions.reason: The question is about the disciples, but it tests the teacher who trains them.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν;

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Not are able the sons of the bridal chamber while the bridegroom with them is to fast?

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "The sons of the bridal chamber cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, can they?
en.B: Jesus answered, "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is there with them?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "When there is a wedding, the groom's friends do not go without food while he is with them.

es.L: Y Jesús les dijo: «¿Acaso pueden los hijos de la cámara nupcial ayunar mientras el novio está con ellos?
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «¿Pueden ayunar los invitados a la boda mientras el novio está con ellos?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Cuando hay una boda, los amigos del novio no dejan de comer mientras él está con ellos.

sw.L: Na Yesu akawaambia, "Je, wana wa ukumbi wa harusi wanaweza kufunga wakati bwana harusi yuko pamoja nao?
sw.B: Yesu aliwajibu, "Je, wageni wa harusi wanaweza kufunga wakati bwana harusi yuko pamoja nao?
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Wakati wa harusi, marafiki wa bwana harusi hawaachi kula wakati yeye yuko pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: the sons of the bridal chamber: the groom's friends and guests at the wedding
decisions.reason: The Semitic phrase "sons of" means those who belong to something. Here they are the bridegroom's attendants and guests.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a wedding was a week of feasting and joy
decisions.reason: No one fasted at a wedding. The guests ate and celebrated with the groom.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The prophets pictured God as Israel's husband (Hosea 2:19-20; Isaiah 62:5). Jesus speaks of himself as the bridegroom, and his time with his disciples as a wedding.

decisions.choice: cannot ... can they? a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The Greek form expects "no".

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: los hijos de la cámara nupcial
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style idiom, as the English Literal does; it means the groom's friends and guests (meaning decision m1). "Hijos" here is the idiom, not a word about men, so it takes no gender span.

decisions.choice: wana wa ukumbi wa harusi
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek idiom, as the English Literal does; it means the groom's friends and guests (meaning decision m1), and Balanced says so. "Wana" is not limited to males, so no gender span is needed, as in Matthew 9:15.

source.text: ὅσον χρόνον ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετ’ αὐτῶν οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν·

records.literal_gloss: As long as time they have the bridegroom with them, not they are able to fast.

en.L: As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they are not able to fast.
en.B: As long as they have the bridegroom with them, fasting is out of the question.
en.R: As long as the groom is there, they cannot fast.

es.L: Todo el tiempo que tienen al novio con ellos, no pueden ayunar.
es.B: Mientras tengan al novio con ellos, el ayuno está fuera de lugar.
es.R: Mientras el novio está allí, no pueden ayunar.

sw.L: Muda wote walio na bwana harusi pamoja nao, hawawezi kufunga.
sw.B: Maadamu bwana harusi yuko pamoja nao, kufunga hakuwezekani hata kidogo.
sw.R: Wakati bwana harusi yuko pale, hawawezi kufunga.

decisions.choice: the answer to the question: they cannot fast
decisions.reason: Jesus answers his own question. Fasting is for mourning, not for a time of joy.

source.text: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Will come but days when will be taken away from them the bridegroom, and then they will fast in that the day.

en.L: But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day.
en.B: But days are coming when the bridegroom will be taken from them; on that day they will fast.
en.R: But a day is coming when the groom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast.

es.L: Pero vendrán días cuando les sea quitado el novio, y entonces ayunarán en aquel día.
es.B: Pero vienen días en que el novio les será quitado; ese día sí ayunarán.
es.R: Pero llegará un día en que se llevarán al novio lejos de ellos. Entonces sí ayunarán.

sw.L: Lakini siku zitakuja atakapoondolewa bwana harusi kutoka kwao, na hapo watafunga siku ile.
sw.B: Lakini siku zinakuja ambapo bwana harusi ataondolewa kwao; siku hiyo watafunga.
sw.R: Lakini siku itafika ambapo bwana harusi atachukuliwa kutoka kwao. Hapo ndipo watafunga.

decisions.choice: taken away: the first hint of Jesus' death
alternatives: the bridegroom leaves on a journey
decisions.reason: The groom does not leave; he is taken. The verb suggests force and loss. Jesus will speak openly of his death from 8:31.

decisions.choice: on that day: the day he is taken, and the time after it
decisions.reason: Mark has "that day" in the singular after "days" in the plural. Then his disciples will mourn and fast.

source.text: Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μή, αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.

records.literal_gloss: No one a patch of cloth unshrunk sews on garment old; if but not, takes away the filling from it, the new from the old, and worse a tear becomes.

en.L: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear is made.
en.B: Nobody sews a piece of new, unshrunk cloth onto an old coat. If they did, the new patch would shrink and tear away from the old cloth, and the hole would get worse.
en.R: People do not use new cloth to fix a hole in old clothes. The new cloth will shrink when it gets wet, and it will tear away from the old cloth. Then the hole will be bigger.

es.L: Nadie cose un remiendo de tela sin encoger sobre un vestido viejo; de lo contrario, el remiendo tira de él, lo nuevo de lo viejo, y se hace una rotura peor.
es.B: Nadie cose un pedazo de tela nueva, sin encoger, en un manto viejo. Si lo hiciera, el remiendo nuevo se encogería y arrancaría parte de la tela vieja, y el roto quedaría peor.
es.R: Nadie usa tela nueva para tapar un agujero en ropa vieja. La tela nueva se encoge cuando se moja, y se desprende de la tela vieja. Entonces el agujero se hace más grande.

sw.L: Hakuna mtu anayeshona kiraka cha kitambaa kisichofuliwa juu ya vazi kuukuu; la sivyo, kiraka kinavuta kutoka kwake, kipya kutoka kwa kikuukuu, na mpasuko unakuwa mbaya zaidi.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu anayeshona kiraka cha kitambaa kipya ambacho hakijasinyaa juu ya vazi kuukuu. Akifanya hivyo, kiraka kipya kitasinyaa na kujivuta kutoka kwenye kitambaa kikuukuu, na tundu litakuwa kubwa zaidi.
sw.R: Watu hawatumii kitambaa kipya kuziba tundu katika nguo kuukuu. Kitambaa kipya kitasinyaa kikilowa maji, na kitajivuta kutoka kwenye kitambaa kikuukuu. Kisha tundu litakuwa kubwa zaidi.

decisions.choice: unshrunk cloth: new woolen cloth that has not yet been washed
decisions.reason: New cloth shrinks the first time it is washed. Sewn onto an old garment, it pulls and tears it.

decisions.choice: the new and the old do not mix: what Jesus brings cannot be added to old ways
decisions.reason: The picture answers the question about fasting: the new time that has come with Jesus does not fit into old practices.

decisions.choice: shrink (B); shrink when it gets wet (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why the patch pulls away, which the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί.

records.literal_gloss: And no one puts wine new into wineskins old; if but not, will burst the wine the skins, and the wine is lost and the skins.

en.L: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and the skins [too].
en.B: And nobody pours new wine into old wineskins. If they did, the wine would split the skins, and both wine and skins would be lost.
en.R: And people do not put new wine into old bags made of skin. The new wine would make the old bags burst, and the wine and the bags would both be lost.

es.L: Y nadie echa vino nuevo en odres viejos; de lo contrario, el vino reventará los odres, y el vino se pierde, y los odres [también].
es.B: Y nadie echa vino nuevo en odres viejos. Si lo hiciera, el vino rompería los odres, y se perderían tanto el vino como los odres.
es.R: Tampoco se pone vino nuevo en bolsas de cuero viejas. El vino nuevo haría reventar las bolsas viejas, y se perderían el vino y las bolsas.

sw.L: Na hakuna mtu anayetia divai mpya katika viriba vikuukuu; la sivyo, divai itavipasua viriba, na divai inapotea, na viriba [pia].
sw.B: Wala hakuna mtu anayemimina divai mpya katika viriba vikuukuu. Akifanya hivyo, divai itavipasua viriba, na divai pamoja na viriba vitapotea.
sw.R: Watu hawaweki divai mpya katika mifuko mikuukuu ya ngozi. Divai mpya ingeipasua mifuko hiyo mikuukuu, na divai pamoja na mifuko vingepotea vyote.

decisions.choice: wineskins: bags made of goat or sheep skin
decisions.reason: New wine was still fermenting and gave off gas. An old skin had lost its stretch and would split.

decisions.choice: the wine and the skins: both are lost
decisions.reason: The Greek ends the sentence with "and the skins", adding them to the loss.

decisions.choice: bags made of skin
decisions.reason: Readable says what a wineskin is.

source.text: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς.

records.literal_gloss: But wine new into wineskins new.

en.L: But new wine [goes] into new wineskins.
en.B: New wine needs new skins.
en.R: New wine must be put into new bags.

es.L: Sino que el vino nuevo [va] en odres nuevos».
es.B: El vino nuevo necesita odres nuevos».
es.R: El vino nuevo hay que ponerlo en bolsas nuevas».

sw.L: Bali divai mpya [hutiwa] katika viriba vipya."
sw.B: Divai mpya inahitaji viriba vipya."
sw.R: Divai mpya inapaswa kuwekwa katika mifuko mipya."

decisions.choice: no verb: a short saying
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb, as a proverb does.

decisions.choice: new: new in age (the wine) and fresh (the skins)
decisions.reason: The two Greek words for new differ slightly; the first means young, the second fresh and unused.

decisions.choice: [goes]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a verb in brackets.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι διὰ τῶν σπορίμων, καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass he on the Sabbaths to pass through the grainfields, and the disciples of him began a way to make plucking the heads of grain.

en.L: And it happened that on the Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through the grainfields, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples began to make [their] way, plucking the heads of grain.
en.B: One Sabbath Jesus was going through the grainfields, and as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples made their way along, they started to pick heads of grain.
en.R: One Sabbath day, Jesus was walking through some fields of grain with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. As they walked, they picked some of the grain to eat.

es.L: Y sucedió que en sábado {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pasaba por los sembrados, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comenzaron a abrir[se] camino arrancando las espigas.
es.B: Un sábado, Jesús pasaba por los sembrados, y mientras {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos avanzaban por el camino, se pusieron a arrancar espigas.
es.R: Un sábado, Jesús caminaba por unos campos sembrados con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Mientras caminaban, arrancaban algunas espigas para comer.

sw.L: Na ikawa siku ya Sabato alikuwa akipita katikati ya mashamba ya nafaka, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaanza kufanya njia wakivunja masuke.
sw.B: Siku moja ya Sabato Yesu alikuwa akipita katika mashamba ya nafaka, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walipokuwa wakitembea njiani, wakaanza kuchuma masuke.
sw.R: Siku moja ya Sabato, Yesu alikuwa akitembea katika mashamba ya nafaka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Walipokuwa wakitembea, walichuma masuke ili wale.

decisions.choice: make their way: walk along a path
alternatives: make a path by trampling the grain
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean making a road, but here it most likely means going along the path while they picked.

decisions.choice: plucking heads of grain: allowed on any day in a neighbor's field
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 23:25 lets a traveler pick grain by hand from a neighbor's field. The question is not taking the grain but doing it on the Sabbath (2:24).

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: on a Sabbath day
decisions.reason: As in 1:21, the plural names a single Sabbath.

decisions.choice: to eat
decisions.reason: Readable says why they picked it, which 2:25 makes clear: they were hungry.

source.text: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἴδε τί ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν;

records.literal_gloss: And the Pharisees were saying to him, Look, why do they on the Sabbaths what not is lawful?

en.L: And the Pharisees were saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not lawful?"
en.B: The Pharisees said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "See there! Why are they doing something on the Sabbath that the law forbids?"
en.R: The Pharisees said to Jesus, "Look! Your followers are breaking the Sabbath law. Why are they doing that?"

es.L: Y los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «Mira, ¿por qué hacen en sábado lo que no es lícito?».
es.B: Los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¡Fíjate! ¿Por qué hacen en sábado algo que la ley prohíbe?».
es.R: Los fariseos le dijeron a Jesús: «¡Mira! Tus discípulos están quebrantando la ley del sábado. ¿Por qué hacen eso?».

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakimwambia, "Tazama, mbona wanafanya siku ya Sabato jambo lisilo halali?"
sw.B: Mafarisayo walimwambia, "Angalia! Kwa nini wanafanya siku ya Sabato jambo ambalo sheria inakataza?"
sw.R: Mafarisayo walimwambia Yesu, "Tazama! Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanavunja sheria ya Sabato. Kwa nini wanafanya hivyo?"

decisions.choice: not lawful: they counted plucking grain as reaping, work forbidden on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The law forbids work on the Sabbath, even at harvest (Exodus 34:21). The Pharisees' teaching counted plucking grain as reaping.

decisions.choice: to him: the teacher is held responsible for his disciples
alternatives: the Pharisees speak to the disciples
decisions.reason: As in 2:18, the complaint about the disciples is brought to Jesus.

decisions.choice: a statement, then why (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the complaint is before asking why.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Never did you read what did David when need he had and was hungry, he and those with him?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him?
en.B: He answered, "Have you not read what David did when he and his men were in need and hungry?
en.R: Jesus answered, "You have read in the Scriptures what David did when he and the men with him were hungry and had nothing to eat.

es.L: Y les dice: «¿Nunca {{plural_you:leyeron|leísteis}} lo que hizo David cuando tuvo necesidad y tuvo hambre, él y los que estaban con él?
es.B: Él les respondió: «¿No {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} lo que hizo David cuando él y sus hombres pasaban necesidad y tenían hambre?
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Ustedes han leído|Vosotros habéis leído}} en las Escrituras lo que hizo David cuando él y sus compañeros tenían hambre y no tenían nada que comer.

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Hamjasoma kamwe alichofanya Daudi alipokuwa na haja na kuona njaa, yeye na wale waliokuwa pamoja naye?
sw.B: Aliwajibu, "Je, hamjasoma alichofanya Daudi, yeye na watu wake, walipokuwa na shida na njaa?
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu, "Mmesoma katika Maandiko kile alichofanya Daudi wakati yeye na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye walipokuwa na njaa, wala hawakuwa na chakula.

decisions.choice: David: the story of 1 Samuel 21:1-6
decisions.reason: David, fleeing from Saul, came to the priest at Nob and asked for bread for himself and his men.

decisions.choice: have you never read? a rebuke to experts in the scriptures
decisions.reason: The Pharisees knew the story well. The question asks why they have not seen what it means.

decisions.choice: a statement: You have read (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question assumes; the question form is kept at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἱερεῖς, καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν;

records.literal_gloss: How he entered into the house of the God in [the time of] Abiathar high priest, and the loaves of the presentation he ate, which not is lawful to eat except for the priests, and he gave also to those with him being?

en.L: How he entered into the house of God in [the time of] Abiathar [the] high priest, and ate the loaves of the presentation, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and he gave also to those who were with him?"
en.B: In the days of Abiathar the high priest, he went into the house of God and ate the bread set out before God, which the law allows only the priests to eat. He even gave some to the men with him."
en.R: In the time of Abiathar the high priest, David went into God's house and ate the special bread that was offered to God. The law says that only the priests may eat that bread. But David ate it, and he gave some to his men too."

decisions.choice: the loaves of the presentation: the bread set out before God
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set on a table in the holy place each Sabbath and eaten by the priests the next week (Leviticus 24:5-9).

decisions.choice: in the time of Abiathar: 1 Samuel 21 names the priest Ahimelech, Abiathar's father
alternatives: Abiathar was the priest who gave the bread
decisions.reason: Abiathar was Ahimelech's son and escaped the slaughter of the priests at Nob (1 Samuel 22:20). He became David's high priest and is better known. The Greek may mean "in the time of Abiathar", or "in the passage about Abiathar", as 12:26 says "at the bush" for a passage. Some manuscripts leave out the phrase.

decisions.choice: the house of God: the tent of worship at Nob
decisions.reason: The temple was not yet built. The house of God was the tabernacle, then at Nob.

decisions.choice: David's need came before the rule
decisions.reason: Even the bread kept for the priests was given to meet human need. Jesus draws the point in 2:27.

decisions.choice: the bread set out before God (B); the special bread that was offered to God (R)
decisions.reason: Older names for the loaves are unclear today; the levels say what the bread was.

decisions.choice: los panes de la presentación (L); el pan puesto delante de Dios (B); el pan especial que se ofrecía a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The bread set out before God in the sanctuary (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the Greek wording; "proposición", the traditional term, now means a proposal to most readers.

decisions.choice: mikate ya kutolewa mbele [ya Mungu] (L); mikate iliyowekwa mbele za Mungu (B); mikate maalum iliyotolewa kwa Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The bread set out before God in the sanctuary (meaning decision m1). Each level says what the bread was in its own way; the traditional phrase is avoided because "wonyesho" (display) no longer explains it.

sw.B: Kisha aliwaambia, "Sabato iliwekwa kwa ajili ya watu, si watu kwa ajili ya Sabato.

decisions.choice: the man: human beings
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, with the article for the whole kind. So the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: the Sabbath was given for people's good
decisions.reason: God gave the Sabbath as rest and blessing (Exodus 20:8-11; Deuteronomy 5:12-15). Rules that turn it into a burden miss its purpose.

decisions.choice: came to be: God made it so
decisions.reason: The verb recalls creation, where God rested and blessed the seventh day (Genesis 2:2-3).

decisions.choice: God made
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who made the Sabbath, following the meaning note.

decisions.choice: mwanadamu (L); watu (B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English puts "humankind" and "man" under the gender setting. "Mwanadamu" and "watu" already mean human beings (meaning decision m1), and "mwanamume" would mean a male and change the sense, so Swahili has nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself
decisions.reason: As in 2:10. Some read it as "a human being", following 2:27, but in Mark it is always Jesus speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: Lord of the Sabbath: he has authority over it
alternatives: he does away with the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The Sabbath belongs to God (Exodus 20:10). Jesus claims the right to say what it is for, as in 2:10 he claims the right to forgive.

decisions.choice: so that: what follows from 2:27
decisions.reason: If the Sabbath is for human good, the Son of Man, who has authority on earth (2:10), rules over it.

decisions.choice: Lord, with a capital
decisions.reason: The word is used here of Jesus' authority over what belongs to God, so it is capitalized, as "Lord" is for Jesus elsewhere.
